# A complete planar receiver for learned ferromagnetic interfaces

2026-11-04. Status: scoped receiver construction; independent review is recorded in PLANAR_RECEIVER_AUDIT.md. Depends on the weighted stability theorem in PROOF.md; that theorem is not modified here. Established matchgate synthesis and FKT are explicitly used, not claimed as new algorithms.

## 1. Input/output contract

There are B isolated unknown zero-field ferromagnetic planar Ising blocks. Block b has k_b ordered boundary spins lying on one face and an empirical pair matrix A_b, obtained from independent isolated-block snapshots. Let C_b be its unknown true pair matrix and D_total=sum_b sum_(i<j)|A_(b,ij)-C_(b,ij)|. The structural promise and boundary order are supplied, not tested.

The assembly is a SUPPLIED PLANAR FACTOR-GRAPH EMBEDDING in a disk. Each block is a node with its k_b ports in the measured cyclic order. Distinct block ports initially correspond to distinct spin variables. Known environment spins and ferromagnetic pair factors (1+a_e x_u x_v), with rational 0<=a_e<=1, connect the ports and environment spins. All environment spins have zero field. Choose K distinct output spins with probe legs on the outer boundary of this same disk, in supplied cyclic order. Boundary fields are allowed only on these cofacial outputs, through product_i(1+t_i x_i), rational 0<=t_i<=1.

The algorithm computes a relative partition-normalization estimate and produces a normalized sampler/evaluator for the K output spins under those fields. Runtime is polynomial in total interface size, known assembly size, field/coupling bit lengths and requested accuracy; it does not depend on unknown internal block volumes. Its guarantee uses D_total and the weighted stability theorem. It does NOT sample arbitrary internal assembly spins, allow general interior fields, or efficiently contract arbitrary nonplanar assemblies.

Use a uniform baseline measure for each explicit environment spin. If physical convention instead sums it with unnormalized counting measure, multiply by the known factor 2 per such spin. Unknown isolated block partition factors are not learned; all outputs are relative to their product.

# Independent audit of the planar receiver

4 November 2026.

Reviewed PLANAR_RECEIVER.md SHA-256: a14bd87344a1d5ba3f8e51ee382061b2d777e3775dc7c6c69cf9114d81b9ba1c.

Dependency PROOF.md SHA-256: c46f70d3ed6e5f4960bfb38fa1f5c3279eb4cecb3ad1c85b44d4820b67597b35. Its weighted relative-error theorem is audited separately in AUDIT.md.

## Verdict and earned extension

The receiver survives this independent adversarial review. It supplies a polynomial-time exact signed contraction oracle for the stated planar/cofacial assemblies, closing a computational gap left open by the abstract weighted stability theorem. Combined with that theorem, it gives the claimed relative normalization estimate and approximate output sampler from noisy isolated-boundary data. No missing Fourier normalization, support/deletion complement, field-parity obstruction, or global Pfaffian sign error was found after checking the actual graph construction.

The theorem is an assembly of established matchgate/FKT machinery with the audited perturbation guarantee. It is not a new general planar solver, does not cover arbitrary nonplanar contractions or interior fields, and does not establish priority, practical advantage or a transformative physical capability.

Before freezing the reviewed version, the author made the inherited sampler conventions explicit: epsilon range, zero-output case, rational-coin cap, positive fallback, nonpositive-root fallback on a failed estimation event, and the no-training M=0 case. These are completeness clarifications, not changes to the central algebra.

## 1. Fourier tensor and normalization

For each block the Fourier expansion already includes 2^−k_b. Introducing uniform measure on its distinct boundary spins and each explicit environment spin therefore leaves no unknown normalization beyond the isolated physical block partition factors, which are explicitly excluded. For each spin, averaging its total Fourier monomial gives one if its exponent is even and zero otherwise. This is exactly the even-parity gate, not twice that gate.

A known edge contributes one for Fourier occupation 00 and a_e for 11, with zero for unequal indices. A block contributes its corresponding principal Pfaffian. # Uniform response learning and stable composition in ferromagnetic environments

2026-11-04. Status: scoped mathematical construction; independent review is recorded separately in AUDIT.md. No priority, general-inference, or transformative-consequence claim.

## 1. Missing operation and precise scope

Ordinary TV accuracy of an isolated block does not control relative partition errors or its response after rare conditioning. Here we prove a stronger statement for a specific environment cone: nonnegative external weights with nonnegative Fourier coefficients. It includes arbitrary-strength ferromagnetic couplings, consistent nonnegative fields, and hard equality constraints. For product boundary fields we give a complete polynomial-time response learner and sampler from passive data. For general environments we prove a composition/error certificate, NOT an unconditional efficient contraction algorithm.

Let P=p_C be a distribution on k ordered spins, with all odd moments zero and all even moments Pf(C_S). Assume additionally that every even moment is nonnegative. These properties hold for free-boundary, zero-field ferromagnetic planar Ising networks, when the observed spins occur in cyclic order on a single face. The hidden bulk graph and its size need not be known.

We receive iid full-boundary samples from this ISOLATED zero-field distribution, not samples of the block embedded in an unknown environment. Correct ordering, equilibrium sampling, and the model promise are assumptions, not conclusions.

For any antisymmetric A define the signed mass
p_A(x)=2^(-k) sum_(S even) Pf(A_S) x_S,
where x_S=product_(i in S)x_i and Pf(empty)=1. It has total mass one. The empirical pair matrix A=C+Delta need not describe a physical model. Set D=sum_(i<j)|Delta_ij|.

An admitted environment weight W is a nonnegative function on the boundary with Fourier expansion
W(x)=sum_S w_S x_S, with every w_S>=0.
Assume Z=E_P W>0. W need not factor across sites and need not be planar.

## 2. Derivative identity

For a matching M of r disjoint index pairs, let U be its endpoints. Differentiating the Pfaffian expansion gives
partial_M p_C(x)=sigma_M 2^(-2r) x_U p_(C_(U complement))(chi x),
where sigma_M is the crossing sign of the selected pairs and chi_l=(-1)^(number of selected arcs whose interiors contain l). A mixed derivative whose selected pairs share an endpoint is zero.

Proof.
